text: ds-cover 是面向 DeepSeek Harness Web 的插件，通过本机 Cover 服务接管 DeepSeek 官方与账号提供方的推理路由，并在页面提供保护状态锁与控制面板。用户可以查看路由和服务状态、启停保护与守护进程、调整并验证 YAML 策略、在本地预览请求转换，也可查看活动元数据和临时实时内容。插件还提供 /cover 命令执行状态查询及常用控制操作。适合希望在使用 DeepSeek Harness 时把请求交给本地 Cover 处理的用户；推理请求最终仍会发送到 DeepSeek。需要预先安装 Cover 可执行程序。

ds-cover routes DeepSeek Harness requests through local Cover and adds a web status panel. Users can manage protection, edit policy, preview transformations, and review activity. A /cover command provides controls. It requires the Cover executable; inference requests still go to DeepSeek.
想让 DeepSeek Harness 的 DeepSeek 请求先经过本地 Cover 处理。
我需要在网页里查看保护状态，并管理 Cover 策略。
I want to inspect how a DeepSeek request is transformed before sending it upstream.
ds-cover 的功能「DeepSeek 请求经 Cover 路由」：把 DeepSeek 官方与账号提供方的推理配置指向本机路由器，再由路由器把请求交给本机 Cover 服务处理。
ds-cover 的功能「网页保护控制面板」：在 DeepSeek Harness Web 页面展示保护状态，并通过面板查看设置检查、管理策略、预览转换和浏览活动信息。
ds-cover 使用前须知：推理请求经本地 Cover 路由后会转发到 api.deepseek.com；连接凭据仍用于 DeepSeek 请求。

ds-cover README · ds-cover：[Cover](https://github.com/DavidCarliez/cover) privacy protection for **DeepSeek Harness Web**. A lock at the bottom of the app shows protection status and opens the control panel.

The plugin routes native DeepSeek API-key and account requests through the real Cover engine. Cover filters sensitive content before it reaches DeepSeek and restores reversible replacements in responses, including streamed text and tool arguments.

ds-cover README · Quick start：**Requires:** DeepSeek Harness **0.2.1-rc.2** (tested), Node.js **22+**, and [Cover **0.3.0+**](https://github.com/DavidCarliez/cover#install). The `cover` executable must be on the harness process's PATH, or set through `COVER_BIN`.

From this repository, run:

```sh
npm ci
npm run build
dsh plugin --profile web add "link:$PWD"
```

Open the harness, click the **Cover** lock, review **Setup checks**, then select **Start**. Alternatively, run `/cover start` in a session.

ds-cover README · Quick start：**Protection starts enabled; automatic fallback starts disabled.** Until the daemon is running, native DeepSeek requests are blocked rather than sent unprotected. Install, restart, or disable the plugin only when no generation is active.

ds-cover README · Using Cover：- **Overview:** toggle protection, manage the daemon, and check setup and health. **Advanced management** contains model downloads and Cover updates/rollbacks.
- **Policy:** edit and validate the full YAML policy, including custom detectors and all six actions: `allow`, `placeholder`, `pseudonymize`, `mask`, `redact`, and `block`. Drafts survive tab switches; closing asks before discarding unsaved changes.
- **Inspect:** preview a request's transformations locally, without sending it to DeepSeek.
- **Activity:** view request metadata, or explicitly enable a temporary live view of sensitive content.

ds-cover README · Using Cover：Saved changes remain marked **pending restart** until Cover reloads them. Starting an already-running daemon does not apply changes. The lock also warns when automatic fallback is enabled, even while Cover is healthy.

The lock describes the selected provider's **next request**, not all traffic on the machine:

ds-cover README · Using Cover：| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Protected | The native route is configured and Cover is healthy. |
| Blocked | Protection is enabled, but the protected route is unavailable. |
| Protection off | Requests bypass Cover. |
| Unprotected fallback | Cover is unavailable and explicitly enabled fallback permits direct requests. |
| Not configured | The selected provider is not supported. |
| Status unknown | The selected provider or current connection status cannot be verified. |

ds-cover README · Using Cover：A failed or policy-blocked request is **never retried directly**. Updates and rollbacks change the shared Cover executable and can affect other integrations. Downloads and executable updates require an explicit action.

Session commands: `/cover status`, `on`, `off`, `start`, `stop`, `restart`, `doctor`, `test`, `monitor`, `fallback on/off`, and `models status/pull`. Prefix each with `/cover`; use the panel for detailed output.

ds-cover README · Configuration and privacy：Runtime files live outside the repository in `~/.local/share/ds-cover`. The policy is at `.config/cover/config.yaml` inside that directory.

On first use, ds-cover validates and imports an existing `~/.config/cover/config.yaml` policy, if present; otherwise it uses Cover's stock defaults. It assigns separate routing, key, and log settings without changing the original configuration or daemon. Later edits to the original policy are not imported automatically.

ds-cover README · Configuration and privacy：**Personal policies, allowlists, keys, and logs are not shipped or committed.** Repository test rules are synthetic. The policy editor changes only the private runtime configuration.

Protection has limits:

ds-cover README · Configuration and privacy：- Only native DeepSeek API-key and account providers are covered. Other providers, shell commands, browser traffic, MCP tools, sign-in, and telemetry are outside this boundary.
- Connection credentials still reach DeepSeek. Images and opaque attachments are not scanned; use `media.images: block` when image content must not leave.
- Previews and opt-in live captures can expose sensitive content to the authenticated browser. Use a trusted connection and avoid screen sharing. Live views clear on connection resets; abandoned views expire within 15 seconds.
- Removing or disabling the plugin restores the underlying provider routing. Stopping only the daemon leaves protection enabled and requests blocked, unless fallback is enabled.
ds-cover README · Configuration and privacy：See [Cover's security boundary](https://github.com/DavidCarliez/cover#security-boundary) for detector and protocol limits.

ds-cover README · Development：```sh
npm test
npm run build
npm run check:package
```

Tests use the real Cover binary and native DeepSeek adapter with temporary policies and loopback upstreams—no cloud model calls. They cover policy actions, streaming/tool restoration, authentication, fail-closed routing, policy activation, and client lifecycle. CI runs on Node.js 22 and 24.

`npm pack` builds bundles automatically. `check:package` verifies a clean-source package and loads its host and client entry points.
ds-cover README · Development：Rebuild after source edits. Client changes reload through the harness; host changes require profile recomposition or restart unless HMR watches this repository.
